# SK3502 — A type owns a disposable field but is not disposable

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

An instance field is constructed by its owner, but the containing type exposes no matching disposal contract.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Lifetime |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

A type that constructs and retains a disposable resource owns its lifetime. If the owner cannot itself be disposed, callers have no reliable point at which to release the retained handle or asynchronously flush it.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
sealed class Store { readonly FileStream stream = new("data", FileMode.Open); }
```

Write:

```csharp
sealed class Store : IDisposable { readonly FileStream stream = new("data", FileMode.Open); public void Dispose() => stream.Dispose(); }
```

## When it does not fire

Ownership is inferred only from a direct object creation in an instance field initializer. Constructor-injected, factory-returned and static fields are ignored because their ownership policy is not knowable locally. A containing type that implements either disposal contract offered by the field — `IDisposable` or `IAsyncDisposable` — is accepted; it need not expose both merely because the resource does. No fix is offered because a correct implementation may need ordering, idempotence, base-class participation and additional owned fields.
